title: Compute brief - 30 October 2026
description: AWS grows 39% to $46.0 billion with a $578 billion backlog and says it will spend meaningfully more than $220 billion next year. Intel Foundry revenue rises 58% to $6.7 billion, but substrate supply caps its packaging ramp, and TSMC is reported to be weighing CoWoS price rises of up to 20%. Canada puts up to C$1.6 billion into Cohere in exchange for C$1.7 billion of compute built at home. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: AWS is selling capacity as fast as it installs it
lede: Amazon closed out hyperscaler earnings week with the same message as Google and Microsoft: demand is ahead of supply. AWS revenue rose 39.3% to $46.0 billion, its fastest growth in nearly five years, its backlog reached $578 billion, more than double a year earlier, and Andy Jassy said AWS is installing an AI accelerator about every 14 seconds with customers taking it almost as fast. Cash capex was $75.9 billion in the quarter; Amazon kept 2026 at about $220 billion and said 2027 will be meaningfully more. Upstream, the squeeze is in packaging: Intel said substrate supply limits how fast it can scale EMIB, and Taiwan press reports TSMC is weighing CoWoS price rises of 10% to 20%. Ottawa turned sovereign AI into a compute obligation, with up to C$1.6 billion of equity in Cohere tied to at least C$1.7 billion of new Canadian computing infrastructure by 2030. On the public tape all 70 list prints confirmed; Lambda H100 holds at $3.99 and B200 at $6.69 per GPU-hour.
